articles.title: Red-sensitive pigments in mantis shrimp eyes act as reversible light switches
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: With about 30 visual pigments, compared to just three in humans, mantis shrimp possess a visual system that remains a mystery. Researchers from ULiège and Humboldt University in Berlin have, for the first time, analyzed these pigments one by one and discovered that some detect red light that very few animals can perceive. This finding, published in Science Advances, has potential applications in optogenetics.

articles.title: Electrical sliding switches graphene between magnetic states
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: In a discovery that could offer a new way to control quantum properties in two-dimensional materials, researchers at Cornell have found that electrically sliding the layers of ultrathin graphene can switch the material between distinct magnetic states that persist even after the voltage is removed.

articles.title: The uranium cubes that exposed Nazi Germany’s nuclear failure
articles.summary: Scientists investigating Nazi Germany's secret nuclear program have uncovered evidence that its final experimental reactor was nowhere near as close to working as previously claimed. Analysis of surviving uranium cubes and wartime documents reveals that Germany lacked the enormous quantities of uranium and heavy water needed to make its reactor operational.
